Rashi on Sukkah 49b:10:1.hebrew: אלא לפי גמילות חסדים שבה - הנתינה היא הצדקה, והטורח הוא החסד: כגון מוליכה לביתו, או טורח שתעלה לו להרבה — כגון נותן לו פת אפויה, או בגד ללבוש, או מעות בעת שהתבואה מצויה, שלא יוציא מעותיו לאיבוד — שנותן לבו ודעתו לטובתו של עני:
Rashi on Sukkah 49b:10:1.english: Only in accordance with the acts of kindness within it - The [act of] giving is the charity, and the exertion is the kindness: such as bringing it to his home, or exerting [oneself] so that it will provide him with great benefit — such as giving him baked bread, or a garment to wear, or money at a time when grain is plentiful, so that he does not spend his money at a loss — for he devotes his heart and mind to the welfare of the poor person.

Rashi on Sukkah 49b:10:2.hebrew: זרעו לכם לצדקה - הצדקה היא הזריעה שזורע כדי לקצור, לקבל שכר. וקצרו לפי חסד — שתקבלו שכר לפי החסד שבה:
Rashi on Sukkah 49b:10:2.english: Sow to yourselves according to charity - Charity is the sowing that one sows in order to reap, [namely] to receive reward. “And reap according to kindness” — that you will receive reward according to the kindness within it.

Rashi on Sukkah 49b:11:1.hebrew: גמילות חסדים בין בגופו - כגון מספיד למת, נושאו, קוברו, משמח חתן, מלוה חבירו בדרך:
Rashi on Sukkah 49b:11:1.english: Acts of kindness, both with his person - Such as eulogizing the dead, carrying him, burying him, gladdening a groom, [and] escorting one's fellow on the road.

Rashi on Sukkah 49b:11:2.hebrew: ובממונו - מלוה לו מעות, משאילו כלים ובהמה:
Rashi on Sukkah 49b:11:2.english: And with his money - He lends him money, [or] lends him utensils and an animal.

Rashi on Sukkah 49b:12:1.hebrew: שמא כל הבא לקפוץ - ולעשות צדקה וחסד, קופץ, ומספיקין וממציאין לו אנשים מהוגנים? לכך ת"ל ״מה יקר״ — צריך לתת לב, ולטרוח ולרדף אחריה, לפי שאינה מצויה תמיד לזכות בה למהוגנים:
Rashi on Sukkah 49b:12:1.english: Lest anyone who comes to leap - and perform charity and kindness, leaps, and worthy people are provided and made available to him? Therefore, the verse states: “How precious” — one must pay attention, and take trouble, and pursue it, because it is not always readily found to merit [performing] it for worthy [recipients].

Rashi on Sukkah 49b:14:1.hebrew: ואמאי נייתי במקודשת - דקא סלקא דעתיה: אין הכלי מקדשן קדושת הגוף ליפסל בלינה, אא"כ דעתו שיקדשנו הכלי; או אם יש בהן יותר מכשיעור — אין ראויין לכלי, ואין הכלי מקדשן, דאין מקדשין אלא הראוי להם:
Rashi on Sukkah 49b:14:1.english: And why? Let him bring [it] in a consecrated [barrel] - For it entered [the questioner's] mind that the vessel does not sanctify them with bodily sanctity, to become disqualified by remaining overnight, unless it is his intention that the vessel sanctify them; or if there is more than the [prescribed] measure in them, they are not fit for the vessel and the vessel does not sanctify them, as [service vessels] only sanctify that which is fit for them.

Rashi on Sukkah 49b:14:2.hebrew: אין שיעור למים - שאפילו יותר משלשה לוגין ראויין לנסך, דלא פירשה בהן תורה שיעורא. הלכך, ראויין לכלי הם, וכלי מיד מקדשם, דכתיב (שמות לא): "כל הנוגע בהם יקדש". ואפילו אינו רוצה שיתקדשו עד מחר — הכלי מקדשן מיד, שלא מדעת:
Rashi on Sukkah 49b:14:2.english: There is no measure for water - For even more than three log are fit for libation, as the Torah did not specify a measure regarding them. Therefore, they are fit for the [sacred] vessel, and the vessel immediately consecrates them, as it is written (Exodus 31): "Whatever touches them shall become holy." And even if one does not wish them to become consecrated until tomorrow, the vessel consecrates them immediately, without intent.

Rashi on Sukkah 49b:1:1.hebrew: מה ניסוכו בקדושה כו' - לא יליף מהכא אלא ששריפתו בקדושה, ולא בחיל חוץ לעזרה. אבל הוצאתו משם פשיטא ליה, כדי שלא יתמלאו, ולא צריך קרא:
Rashi on Sukkah 49b:1:1.english: Just as its pouring is in sanctity, etc. - He derives from here only that its burning [must be] in sanctity, and not in the cheil outside the Courtyard. But its removal from there is obvious to him, so that [the drainpipes] will not become filled, and does not require a verse.

Rashi on Sukkah 49b:1:2.english: From where is it inferred - [How is] burning [inferred] from here?

Rashi on Sukkah 49b:1:3.english: It is derived [from] “sanctity” [and] “sanctity” - And it can also be said that the mitzvah of its removal and its burning is derived from here.

Rashi on Sukkah 49b:2:1.hebrew: בתחילה מועלין בהם - משהוקדשו עד שנתנסכו, יש בהם מעילה, דקדשי גבוה נינהו:
Rashi on Sukkah 49b:2:1.english: Initially, one can misuse consecrated property with them - From [the time] they were consecrated until they were poured as libations, the prohibition of misuse applies to them, for they are the consecrated property of the Most High.

Rashi on Sukkah 49b:2:2.english: [Once] they descended to the drainpipes, one does not misuse consecrated property with them - For there is no need of the Most High in them whatsoever.

Rashi on Sukkah 49b:2:3.hebrew: כמאן - איצטריך למיתני "אין מועלין"? כר' אלעזר בר צדוק, דאין יורדין לתהום, ואפשר לירד ולהביאם:
Rashi on Sukkah 49b:2:3.english: In accordance with whose [opinion] - Was it necessary to teach "one does not misuse [them]"? In accordance with Rabbi Elazar bar Tzadok, for they do not descend to the depths, and it is possible to go down and bring them [up].

Rashi on Sukkah 49b:3:1.english: That it was caught - If one suspended a vessel inside the drainpipes and collected [the wine].

Rashi on Sukkah 49b:4:1.hebrew: א"ד לימא - הא דקתני ״ירדו לשיתין אין מועלין״ — רבנן היא, ואיקלט — אין מועלין, דאין בהן מעתה צורך גבוה. דאי ר' אלעזר — אכתי בקדושתייהו קיימי, דקאמ' ״שורפין אותו בקדושה״, אלמא קדושתו עליהם מדבעו שריפה:
Rashi on Sukkah 49b:4:1.english: Some say: Let us say - That which is taught: “[Once] they descended to the drainpipes, one does not misuse them” — is [in accordance with] the Rabbis; and [if] it was caught, one does not misuse [them], for from now on they have no purpose for the Most High. For if [it were in accordance with] Rabbi Elazar, they would still retain their sanctity, as he said: “They burn it in sanctity” — evidently their sanctity remains upon them, since they require burning.

Rashi on Sukkah 49b:4:2.english: Whose mitzvah has been performed - And its libation is the essence of its mitzvah.

Rashi on Sukkah 49b:4:3.hebrew: פוקקין את השיתין - את נקב שבראש המזבח, שהנסכים יורדין בו לשיתין, שיראה היין עליו כגרון מלא ושבע:
Rashi on Sukkah 49b:4:3.english: They plug the drainpipes - [That is,] the opening at the top of the altar through which the libations descend into the drainpipes, so that the wine will appear upon it like a full and sated throat.

Rashi on Sukkah 49b:4:4.english: Strong drink [shekhar] - An expression of intoxication, joy, and libation.

Rashi on Sukkah 49b:5:1.hebrew: מגרוניה שבע - ע"י ששותהו בלגימות גסות וגרון מלא הוא משביע, ולא על ידי שתיה מרובה שמכניס הרבה יין במעיו ע"י לגימות דקות. ואינן כאוכלין, ששובע שלהם בא במילוי כרס:
Rashi on Sukkah 49b:5:1.english: He is satiated from his throat - By drinking it in large gulps and with a full throat it satiates, and not through copious drinking whereby he introduces much wine into his innards through small sips. And [drinks] are not like foods, whose satiation comes from filling the belly.

Rashi on Sukkah 49b:5:2.english: Swallow in swigs - In large gulps.

Rashi on Sukkah 49b:5:3.hebrew: מגמע ליה גמועי - דרך שביעה, משום חיבוב מצוה:
Rashi on Sukkah 49b:5:3.english: Would swallow it in [large] swigs - In the manner of satiation, out of affection for the mitzvah.

Rashi on Sukkah 49b:6:1.english: In sandals - During the pilgrimage of the Festivals.

Rashi on Sukkah 49b:6:2.english: Prince - For his heart moved him to recognize his Creator.

Rashi on Sukkah 49b:6:3.english: First of the converts - Out of the willingness of his heart to convert.

Rashi on Sukkah 49b:7:1.hebrew: מאי דכתיב חמוקי ירכיך וגו' למה נמשלו וכו' - רב ענן דרש לקרא: ״כמו חלאים״ — כלוחות שהיו מאבנים טובות, כמו ״נזם [זהב] וחלי כתם״ (משלי כ״ה:י״ב); ״מעשה ידי אמן״ — והלוחות ״מעשה אלהים״ (שמות ל״ב:ט״ז):
Rashi on Sukkah 49b:7:1.english: What is that which is written: “The hidden of your thighs,” etc., why are [matters of Torah] likened, etc. - Rav Anan expounded the verse [as referring to the Torah]: “Like ornaments” — like the Tablets, which were of precious stones, as in [the verse]: “A ring of [gold] and an ornament of fine gold” (Proverbs 25:12); “the handiwork of a craftsman” — and the Tablets [are] “the work of God” (Exodus 32:16).

Rashi on Sukkah 49b:7:2.hebrew: חמוקי ירכיך - הנסתרים כירך, שכבוד התורה בצנעא, ולא להיות יושב ושונה בגובה של עיר, ולא לשנות לתלמידיו בשוק, כדאמר במועד קטן (דף טז.):
Rashi on Sukkah 49b:7:2.english: The hidden of your thighs - [Those matters] concealed like a thigh, for the honor of the Torah is in private, and not to be sitting and studying on the heights of a city, nor to teach his students in the marketplace, as it is said in Moed Katan (daf 16a):

Rashi on Sukkah 49b:8:1.hebrew: הוצאת המת והכנסת כלה - דכתיב בהו "לכת": "טוב ללכת אל בית אבל מלכת אל בית משתה" (קהלת ז׳:ב׳). אף שם צריך הצנע: לסעוד במדה נאה ולשמוח במדה נאה, ולא להנהיג קלות ראש בעצמו. וי"א: אם צריך לבזבז להוצאת מת עני או להכנסת כלה ענייה — יעשה בצנעא, ולא לימא קמי מאן דלא ידע דעבדי [כן]. וכן מפרש בשאלתות דרב אחאי:
Rashi on Sukkah 49b:8:1.english: Taking out the dead and bringing in a bride - For "going" is written concerning them: "It is better to go to a house of mourning than to go to a house of feasting" (Ecclesiastes 7:2). Even there, modesty is required: to dine in a decorous manner and to rejoice in a decorous manner, and not to conduct oneself with levity. And some say: If one needs to spend [money] for the funeral of a poor deceased person or for bringing a poor bride [to the wedding canopy], he should do so discreetly, and not say before someone who does not know that he did [so]. And so it is explained in the She'iltot of Rav Achai.

Rashi on Sukkah 49b:8:2.hebrew: דברים שדרכן לעשותן בצנעא - כגון צדקה הניתנת לעני בסתר, שאין צריך להודיע לשום אדם; מה שאין כן במת ובכלה, לפי שאחרים מתעסקין בהן ויודעין היציאה משל מי. והיינו דאמר רבי אלעזר, דכל מילי בעי צניעותא, והוא הדין לדברי תורה:
Rashi on Sukkah 49b:8:2.english: Matters that tend to be conducted in private - Such as charity given to a poor person in secret, where there is no need to inform anyone; which is not the case with [taking out] the dead and [accompanying] a bride, since others are involved with them and know whose expenditure it is. And this is what Rabbi Elazar said: that all matters require modesty, and the same applies to words of Torah.

Rashi on Sukkah 49b:9:1.hebrew: נבחר לה' מזבח - הכל בכלל זבח: חטאת ואשם, ועולה ושלמים — כולם זבח הם:
Rashi on Sukkah 49b:9:1.english: Is more acceptable to the Lord than an offering - All [types of offerings] are included in [the term] sacrifice: sin-offering and guilt-offering, and burnt-offering and peace-offerings — they are all a sacrifice.

Rashi on Sukkah 49b:9:2.hebrew: שנאמר זרעו לכם לצדקה וגו' - קרא הכתוב לזריעה צדקה, ואת החסד קרא קציר, וטובה קצירה מזריעה, כדמפרש:
Rashi on Sukkah 49b:9:2.english: As it is stated: “Sow to yourselves according to charity...” - The verse calls sowing “charity,” and calls kindness “reaping”; and reaping is better than sowing, as [the Gemara] explains:

Rashi on Sukkah 49b:9:3.hebrew: אדם זורע כו' - ספק אינו אוכל — שמא לא יצמח, או ילקה בשדפון וברד:
Rashi on Sukkah 49b:9:3.english: [If] a person sows, etc. - [It is] uncertain whether he will not eat — lest it not sprout, or be stricken by blight or hail.

Tosafot on Sukkah 49b:2:1.hebrew: נסכים בתחילה מועלין בהם - משנה היא במעילה, פרק ולד חטאת (מעילה דף יא.), ומסיק עלה בגמ' בלשונות אחרים שאין כתובים כאן, וגירסא דהכא עיקר:
Tosafot on Sukkah 49b:2:1.english: "[With regard to] libations, initially, one can misuse consecrated property with them" - It is a mishna in Meilah, in the chapter [entitled] Valad Chatat (Meilah 11a), and [the Gemara] concludes about it in the Gemara with other versions that are not written here; and the textual version here is primary.
